social.title: Dai Pai Dong Beers on Temple Street
social.description: Plastic stools on the tarmac at the Yau Ma Tei end of the night market, where the clay-pot rice and typhoon-shelter crab come with large bottles of cold lager.
social.bonus: Order one dish none of you can identify from the Chinese-only board.

social.title: Cocktails at Felix, The Peninsula
social.description: Philippe Starck's 1994 room on the 28th floor of The Peninsula — the first restaurant in Asia he designed, with floor-to-ceiling glass facing the island.
social.bonus: Find the men's room urinals with the window view, whether or not you need them.

social.title: Hong Kong Observation Wheel After Dark
social.description: A 60-metre wheel parked on the Central harbourfront for the price of a coffee, turning three or four times while the ferries cross underneath.
social.bonus: Ride it twice in a row without getting out, which the ticket lets you do.

social.title: Butterfly Ceiling at The Iron Fairies
social.description: An ironsmith's workshop of a bar with 10,000 preserved butterflies strung from the ceiling, hidden under the Chinachem building with the door on Pottinger Street.
social.bonus: Sit at the forge end of the bar and count how long before you spot the live jazz set starting.

social.title: Neway Karaoke Box in Tsim Sha Tsui
social.description: A private karaoke room with a buffet and a Cantopop catalogue going back decades, booked by the hour at the chain Hong Kong has sung in for over 20 years.
social.bonus: Everyone has to sing one Cantopop song, in Cantonese, however badly.

social.title: Live Band Night at The Wanch
social.description: Hong Kong's longest-running live music room, where local bands have played to a crowd of 30 since 1987, now refurbished with a proper sound system and a kitchen.
social.bonus: Stay for the band you have never heard of, not just the headline act.

social.title: House Band at Ned Kelly's Last Stand
social.description: A Kowloon dive opened in 1972 where the same jazz and blues band plays trad standards every single night, led by the same man since 1998.
social.bonus: Request a standard the band has to argue about before they play it.

social.title: Ozone on the 118th Floor
social.description: The highest rooftop bar on the planet, 490 metres up on top of the ICC, where the cloud sometimes closes over the terrace while you are still holding the drink.
social.bonus: Get a seat on the open-air terrace, not inside, whatever the weather is doing.

social.title: Craft Beer at The Globe
social.description: The pub that started Hong Kong's craft beer habit, with the city's longest tap list and local brands like Black Kite and Moonzen pouring beside the pies.
social.bonus: Drink only beers brewed in Hong Kong for the whole session.

social.title: Molecular Cocktails at Quinary
social.description: Antonio Lai's lab on Hollywood Road, where the Earl Grey Caviar Martini arrives under a cloud of tea foam and spherified pearls, and has done since 2012.
social.bonus: Order the Earl Grey Caviar Martini first, then let the bartender choose your second.

social.title: Gin Flight at Ping Pong 129 Gintonería
social.description: An unmarked red door in Sai Ying Pun opening onto a cavernous old table-tennis hall, now stocked with more than 120 gins and hung with local art.
social.bonus: Find the door without looking it up, then let the bartender pick the gin.

social.title: Wednesday Night Racing at Happy Valley
social.description: Midweek horse racing in a floodlit bowl ringed by apartment towers, with a beer garden on the infield and 25,000 people shouting down the straight.
social.bonus: Put the minimum bet on the horse with the worst name, every race, no exceptions.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Next Ferry Out of Central
8ball.description: Walk to the Central piers, board whichever outlying-island ferry leaves next — Peng Chau, Lamma, Cheung Chau, Discovery Bay — and spend the afternoon wherever it puts you.
8ball.bonus: No looking up the island before you land. Find lunch by walking.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Cooked Food Centre Roulette
8ball.description: Go up to the cooked food centre on the top floor of a municipal market building and each order from the stall with the longest local queue — no menu reading, no discussion.
8ball.bonus: Eat everything that arrives at the table. All of it. No swapping.

culture.title: Tai Kwun, the Old Central Police Station
culture.description: Sixteen restored colonial buildings, a Victorian prison yard and two aluminium-skinned art blocks, all stitched into one free compound above Hollywood Road.
culture.bonus: Stand inside one of the original D Hall cells with the door shut.

culture.title: Ping Shan Heritage Trail
culture.description: A one-kilometre walk through 800 years of Tang clan territory in Yuen Long, taking in ancestral halls, a study hall and Hong Kong's only surviving ancient pagoda.
culture.bonus: Climb what you can of Tsui Sing Lau Pagoda and read the clan names in the hall.

culture.title: Incense Coils at Man Mo Temple
culture.description: An 1847 temple to the gods of literature and war, so thick with hanging incense coils that the light comes through in bars, a block off the antiques street.
culture.bonus: Read the two sedan chairs' inscriptions before you leave, then walk Cat Street.

culture.title: Sam Tung Uk Walled Village Museum
culture.description: A complete 18th-century Hakka walled village, furnished room by room as it was lived in, marooned among the tower blocks of Tsuen Wan.
culture.bonus: Stand in the central ancestral hall and work out how 200 people shared this space.

culture.title: Hong Kong Museum of Art, Tsim Sha Tsui
culture.description: Chinese antiquities, Xubaizhai scroll paintings and the Chater collection of colonial-era China trade art, in a rebuilt harbour-front museum with glass stairwells over the water.
culture.bonus: Find the 19th-century painting of the harbour and compare it with the view out the window.

culture.title: Cantonese Opera at the Xiqu Centre
culture.description: Painted faces, falsetto and clashing gongs in a purpose-built opera house whose Grand Theatre is suspended 27 metres up, so the street noise never reaches it.
culture.bonus: Go in knowing nothing about the plot and work it out from the costumes alone.

culture.title: M+ Museum, West Kowloon
culture.description: Asia's first global museum of contemporary visual culture, a Herzog and de Meuron slab on the harbour holding the Sigg collection of Chinese contemporary art.
culture.bonus: Find the Sigg Prize gallery and pick the one piece you would hang at home.

culture.title: Hong Kong Palace Museum
culture.description: Rotating loans from Beijing's Forbidden City — imperial robes, jades and court paintings — inside a gold-toned building shaped like a ritual vessel.
culture.bonus: Work out which three objects in the room you would smuggle out, then move on.

chill.title: Star Ferry Crossing at Dusk
chill.description: Eight minutes across Victoria Harbour on a green-and-white ferry running since 1888, for the price of a bottle of water, as the towers switch their lights on.
chill.bonus: Pay the extra for the upper deck and sit on the open bow bench, facing the island.

chill.title: Repulse Bay Afternoon
chill.description: The south side's wide crescent of imported sand, backed by the wave-shaped apartment block with a hole through its middle, 20 minutes from Central by bus.
chill.bonus: Walk to the Kwun Yam shrine at the far end and cross the little wishing bridge.

chill.title: Nan Lian Garden and Chi Lin Nunnery
chill.description: A Tang-dynasty garden of rock, water and bonsai built to classical rules, next to a nunnery assembled entirely from interlocking cypress with no nails at all.
chill.bonus: Find the golden pavilion's reflection in the pond and work out where the water goes.

chill.title: Kowloon Walled City Park
chill.description: A Jiangnan-style garden laid out over the footprint of the densest settlement on earth, with the old yamen building and excavated gates left in place.
chill.bonus: Find the bronze model of the Walled City and locate where its rooftops would have been.

chill.title: Fortune Lane at Wong Tai Sin Temple
chill.description: Smoke, drums and the rattle of bamboo fortune sticks at Hong Kong's busiest working temple, with a whole arcade of soothsayers behind it.
chill.bonus: Shake the chim until one stick falls out, then have it read in Fortune Telling Lane.

chill.title: Edward Youde Aviary in Hong Kong Park
chill.description: A walk-through rainforest aviary dropped into a valley in the middle of Admiralty, with 600 birds overhead and skyscrapers behind the mesh.
chill.bonus: Stay on the elevated walkway until you have spotted five species you cannot name.

chill.title: Top Deck of the Ding Ding, End to End
chill.description: The whole length of the island's north shore on a double-deck tram from 1904, front seat on top, at walking pace through Wan Chai and North Point.
chill.bonus: Ride Kennedy Town to Shau Kei Wan without getting off, front row upstairs.

chill.title: Morning Tai Chi in the Zoological and Botanical Gardens
chill.description: Hong Kong's oldest park, open since 1871 on the slope above Central, where retirees run through tai chi forms under the fig trees at first light.
chill.bonus: Join the back row of a tai chi group and copy the whole sequence without asking.

chill.title: Hong Kong Wetland Park Boardwalks
chill.description: Sixty hectares of mangrove and mudflat on the edge of Deep Bay, with hides looking across the water at Shenzhen's skyline and migrating waders in between.
chill.bonus: Sit in the floating hide for ten silent minutes and count what lands.

chill.title: Symphony of Lights from the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade
chill.description: Forty-odd buildings on both shores firing lasers and searchlights in time to music at 20:00, watched from the harbour railing on the Kowloon side.
chill.bonus: Get there 30 minutes early, claim the railing at the Avenue of Stars, and stay put.

foodie.title: Wonton Noodles at Mak's Noodle, Wellington Street
foodie.description: A teacup-sized bowl of springy noodles under four prawn wontons, made by the family that has done nothing else in Central for over 60 years.
foodie.bonus: Eat it the local way — noodles first, before they soften, and do not add soy.

foodie.title: Dim Sum at Tim Ho Wan, Sham Shui Po
foodie.description: Baked barbecue pork buns with a sugar-crackle top, from the Sham Shui Po dim sum shop that has been in the Michelin guide for 17 straight years.
foodie.bonus: Order three baked pork buns for the table, then order three more.

foodie.title: Beef Brisket Noodles at Kau Kee
foodie.description: Brisket braised to collapse in a broth the same family has kept going on Gough Street since the 1930s, with a queue down the pavement most of the day.
foodie.bonus: Order the curry brisket, not the clear broth, and share a table with a stranger.

foodie.title: Roast Goose at Yat Lok, Stanley Street
foodie.description: Lacquered roast goose over rice in a cramped Central shophouse, built on a 20-step method the family has run since 1957 and a Michelin star held since 2015.
foodie.bonus: Order the lower leg, not the breast, and finish the skin first.

foodie.title: Char Siu at Joy Hing, Wan Chai
foodie.description: Charcoal-edged barbecued pork over rice from a Wan Chai roast shop trading since 1938, where the counter hooks empty out by mid-afternoon.
foodie.bonus: Ask for the fatty cut, half char siu and half roast goose on one plate.

foodie.title: Scrambled Eggs at Australia Dairy Company
foodie.description: The most famously brusque breakfast in Hong Kong — cloud-soft scrambled eggs, buttered toast and steamed milk pudding, served at a speed that borders on hostile.
foodie.bonus: Order, eat and pay in under fifteen minutes without being told to hurry.

foodie.title: Egg Tarts at Tai Cheong Bakery, Lyndhurst Terrace
foodie.description: Shortcrust egg tarts baked since 1954, still sold warm out of the tray at the original Central shop that the last colonial governor queued at.
foodie.bonus: Eat the first one standing on the pavement while it is still too hot.

foodie.title: Tomato Noodles at Sing Heung Yuen Dai Pai Dong
foodie.description: One of the last licensed dai pai dongs in Central, cooking under a tin roof on a stepped lane since 1957, famous for tomato soup noodles and crisp honey-butter toast.
foodie.bonus: Get the tomato noodles with beef and a crispy bun, and eat at the roadside table.

foodie.title: Pineapple Bun and Milk Tea at Kam Wah Café
foodie.description: The city's benchmark bo lo bao — a crackle-topped bun split around a cold slab of butter — at a cha chaan teng that has not changed since 1973.
foodie.bonus: Order it bo lo yau, with the butter, and do not ask for it without.

foodie.title: Dim Sum at Lung King Heen
foodie.description: Cantonese dim sum at harbour level in the Four Seasons, the first Chinese restaurant in the world to be given three Michelin stars, and still a two-star room today.
foodie.bonus: Book the lunch sitting and ask for a window table on Victoria Harbour.

adventure.title: Tai Mo Shan Summit Before Dawn
adventure.description: The highest ground in Hong Kong at 957 metres, where the cloud sits below you at dawn and the temperature runs ten degrees under the city.
adventure.bonus: Take a jumper you think you will not need. You will need it.

adventure.title: Cheung Chau Mini Great Wall
adventure.description: A granite walkway along the cliffs of a dumbbell-shaped island, threading past wind-cut rocks with names like the Human Head and the Reclining Rock.
adventure.bonus: Find the pirate cave at Cheung Po Tsai and go in as far as your phone torch lasts.

adventure.title: Lamma Island Family Trail Crossing
adventure.description: A car-free island crossed on foot from one ferry pier to the other, over a ridge, past a swimming beach, and down into a seafood village.
adventure.bonus: Walk it in the opposite direction to everyone else, from Sok Kwu Wan to Yung Shue Wan.

adventure.title: Kam Shan Monkey Hill Reservoir Loop
adventure.description: A colonial reservoir circuit 20 minutes from Mong Kok with several hundred rhesus macaques living along it, entirely unbothered by you.
adventure.bonus: Walk the whole loop without a monkey getting into your bag.

adventure.title: Tai O Stilt Village Walk
adventure.description: A Tanka fishing village on stilts over a tidal creek on far west Lantau, where shrimp paste still dries on the rooftops and the drawbridge is cranked by hand.
adventure.bonus: Buy something dried off a rooftop rack and eat it before you leave the village.

adventure.title: The Twins Stairs on Wilson Trail Stage 1
adventure.description: Over 1,100 stone steps straight up two peaks above Stanley — the cruellest staircase in Hong Kong, and the reason local hikers train here.
adventure.bonus: No sitting down until the second summit. Standing rests only.

adventure.title: Bride's Pool and Plover Cove Reservoir
adventure.description: A chain of waterfalls and plunge pools in the far northeast, paired with the dam wall of a reservoir built by sealing off a whole sea inlet.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full length of the main dam and look back at where the sea used to be.

adventure.title: World of Frozen at Hong Kong Disneyland
adventure.description: The first Arendelle ever built, a whole fjord village with a runaway sleigh coaster, inside the park Hong Kong reaches by its own dedicated MTR line.
adventure.bonus: Ride Wandering Oaken's Sliding Sleighs in the front row with your hands up.

adventure.title: Summit Cable Car and Arctic Blast at Ocean Park
adventure.description: A 1977 marine park built across a headland, where the ride between halves is a cable car strung over the open sea and the best coaster is a spinning one on the Summit.
adventure.bonus: Take the cable car up and the Ocean Express tunnel down, so you get both.

adventure.title: Dragon's Back Ridge to Big Wave Bay
adventure.description: A knife-edge ridge 15 minutes from the city that drops you onto the surf beach at Big Wave Bay, with the South China Sea on both sides the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Walk it east to west and swim at Big Wave Bay before you catch the bus back.

adventure.title: Ngong Ping 360 Crystal Cabin to the Big Buddha
adventure.description: A 5.7km cable car with a glass floor, swinging over the bay and up Lantau's spine to the 34-metre bronze Tian Tan Buddha and the 268 steps to its feet.
adventure.bonus: Climb all 268 steps without stopping, then ring the bell at the top.

adventure.title: Lantau Peak Sunrise Climb
adventure.description: Hong Kong's second-highest peak, climbed in the dark from Pak Kung Au so you are standing at 934 metres when the sun comes up over the Pearl River Delta.
adventure.bonus: Carry breakfast up and eat it on the summit before you start down to the Big Buddha.

adventure.title: Sai Wan to Tai Long Wan Beach Hike
adventure.description: Four empty white-sand bays strung along the Sai Kung coast, reachable only on foot, and the closest thing Hong Kong has to a desert island.
adventure.bonus: Swim at Ham Tin, then eat at the beach shack before the last boat.

adventure.title: Lion Rock Summit at Golden Hour
adventure.description: A steep scramble up the lion's head above Kowloon, where the whole peninsula lines up under you as the light goes orange.
adventure.bonus: Stand on the lion's nose for the photo — then put the phone away for ten minutes.

adventure.title: High Island Reservoir East Dam Columns
adventure.description: Hexagonal volcanic columns 100 metres tall, folded like a collapsed accordion, in a UNESCO Global Geopark at the far end of a sea wall of dolosse.
adventure.bonus: Walk down to the sea cave at the foot of the columns if the tide allows.

adventure.title: Old Peak Road Climb to Victoria Peak
adventure.description: The 1860s sedan-chair route up the mountain — a relentless concrete ramp through the jungle that skips the tram queue entirely.
adventure.bonus: Beat the tram: send someone up by rail and race them from Central.
